title: Dialogue Seed Lab Journal
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for experiments around 'dialogue seeding' — i.e., small, structured examples and short priming snippets used to shape multi-turn assistant behavior with constrained token budgets. Primary goal: find repeatable, compact seed patterns that improve consistency (role fidelity, answer format) across variable prompts and model sizes while keeping token cost low.

Background / motivation:
- Many product prompts are brittle when users deviate from the happy path. We want compact seeds that are robust to: user role-switching, code snippets in the query, and partial instructions.
- Constraints: 1) favor <150 token added seeding overhead, 2) work across open models we serve (variants of Llama-like and Mistral-like families), 3) tolerate temperature variation up to 0.8.

Experiment categories (high level):
- Persona anchor seeds: 1–3 short instructions about style/role (tone, expertise).
- Examples-as-turns: 2–4 short multi-turn examples that show expected pattern (user -> assistant pairs).
- Meta-directives: explicit rules ("always return JSON", "do not invent facts").
- Failback clauses: short fallback instruction to trigger safe-guarding when model hallucinates.

Seed templates (compact variants):
1) Persona-Only (anchor):
[system] You are an expert product analyst. Be concise, cite assumptions.
[user] Q: {user_query}

2) Mini-Conversation (2-shot single-line):
[user] How do I A?
[assistant] Step 1: X. Step 2: Y.
[user] {user_query}

3) JSON-Output Directive (meta + example):
[system] Format your reply as valid JSON with keys: summary, steps, confidence.
[user] Q: What now?
[assistant] {"summary": "...", "steps": ["..."], "confidence": "low/high"}
[user] {user_query}

4) Anchored-Fallback (safety short):
[system] If you are unsure, say: "I don't have enough info" instead of inventing details.
[user] {user_query}

Compact few-shot set (for testing):
- Example A: user asks budgeting question; assistant responds (3–4 short bullets).
- Example B: user asks to rewrite email; assistant responds formal->concise mapping.
- Example C: user asks ambiguous ask; assistant asks clarification question.

Three concrete few-shot recipes (for playbook):
Recipe alpha — role + 1-shot: combine Persona-Only + Example A. (~100 tokens)
Recipe beta — JSON directive + 2-shot: ensures structured outputs (useful for downstream parsing). (~130 tokens)
Recipe gamma — fallback-heavy: anchored-fallback + clarification example to reduce hallucinations. (~90 tokens)

Observed failure modes (notes from quick runs):
- Role drift after long context (assistant slowly slips to generic helper after ~5 user turns).
- JSON directive sometimes ignored if user includes codeblock in the query; model prefers to mimic code.
- Clarification generation: when seed includes explicit clarifying example, model tends to ask a question even when user was explicit — overfitting to the example.
- Conflicting instructions: persona says "concise" while example shows long justification -> model mixes styles.

Diagnostics and quick checks:
- Turn window tests: run seeds with synthetic 8-turn dialogues to measure drift probability (binary: preserved role after turn N).
- Token budget check: compute added seed tokens across model tokenization (gpt2-like BPE) and flag if >150 tokens.
- Stability sweep: temperatures [0.0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8], top_p [0.7, 0.9], for each seed-template across 3 model variants (small/medium/large).
- Failure reproducibility: capture seed + deterministic random seed (sampling) so we can replay hallucinations with same prompt/seed for triage.

Example test cases (realistic snippets):
(1) Ambiguous ask: "Plan a 2-week onboarding for a midlevel PM." Expected: ask about team size/role scope unless user included details.
(2) Rewrite w/ constraints: "Make this email 3 sentences, friendly, and add a subject line." Expected: subject + 3-sentence body.
(3) Data question w/ code: "Explain why this SQL returns duplicates." Expected: short diagnostic steps; do not fabricate table schema.

Mini-results (notes from 2026-02 micro-run):
- Recipe beta (JSON directive) worked best for downstream parser on medium model; median validity 86% at temp 0.2, drops to 58% at temp 0.8.
- Recipe gamma reduced hallucination phrases by ~30% on small model but increased clarification prompts by 12% (tradeoff).
- Persona-Only is cheapest but least robust; role drift often occurs by turn 4.

Open hypotheses to test next:
- H1: Short explicit clarification example reduces inappropriate assumptions more than a generic "ask clarification" meta-rule.
- H2: JSON directives should be placed in system message rather than user message to improve compliance under high temp.
- H3: Alternating the example order (example showing clarification first vs second) affects tendency to ask clarifying Qs.

Planned experiments (2-week sprint):
- Sprint week 1: run stability sweep for Recipe alpha/beta/gamma across 3 models with metrics: format_validity, hallucination_rate, clarification_rate, token_overhead.
- Sprint week 2: tune templates (truncate examples, move directives to system slot) and run ablation where we remove persona or example to measure contribution.

Evaluation heuristics (quick):
- Format_validity: boolean if output matches required JSON / subject line / bullet structure.
- Hallucination_rate: presence of unverifiable facts (binary per reply), annotated by labeler or heuristic.
- Clarification_rate: fraction of replies that ask for clarification.
- Style_match: length/brevity score relative to requirement.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add tokenizer-length estimates for each seed (run with our tokenizer script).
- Wire up a small harness to sweep temp + seed combos on Dedicated sandbox. Ticket: INF-1015.
- Draft short internal guide: "When to use JSON directive vs persona anchors" — aim for 1 page.
- Share initial results with Solutions Eng for customer-facing templates (Owen).

Quick links / references:
- confluence:dialogue-seed-refactor (design doc for seed placement)
- GH:inference/seed-templates PR#482 (current test harness)
- JIRA:INF-973 (bug: JSON directive ignored for codeblock inputs)

Random notes and heuristics (brain-dump):
- Prefer 1 short example that demonstrates asking for missing critical info rather than many examples.
- Avoid mixing style constraints (concise/detailed) in the same seed. Pick one anchor and ensure examples reflect it.
- Consider small regex post-filter to catch invalid JSON instead of inflating seed size to guarantee compliance.

End of entry.

Last quick checklist before next run:
- [ ] Tokenize seeds and record sizes
- [ ] Add deterministic replay ids to harness outputs
- [ ] Prepare ablation list for persona vs example vs directive
- [ ] Sync with Owen about customer templates
